goal: Define a documentation-only replacement plan for the current TaskGraph bottom-layer scheduler with a scalable Chase-Lev work-stealing scheduler, while preserving existing GraphEvent semantics, dependency behavior, and Next chaining behavior.

current_limits: Current wake-up bookkeeping in TaskFIFOQueue uses a 32-bit bitmap path (LockFree.h) and fixed-priority queue layout, creating scaling pressure when worker topology grows.
TaskGraph worker scheduling is tightly coupled to priority-indexed shared queues, and wake/park behavior is simplistic for modern high-core systems.
Current backend is difficult to evolve independently because task/event semantics and scheduler mechanics are not clearly separated.
problem_statement.target_outcome: Replace only the bottom-layer scheduler with a work-stealing design so upper-layer task graph behavior remains functionally equivalent.

goals: Introduce per-worker Chase-Lev deques for local push/pop and cross-worker stealing.
Support dynamic deque growth; resizing can use a lock because it is not in the hottest steady-state path.
Keep GraphEvent prerequisite accounting, AddSubsequent/TryUnlockSubsequents behavior, and GraphTask::CreateInfo::Next chaining semantics unchanged.
Make Scheduler independent of GraphEventRef and GraphEvent internals.
Keep TaskGraph as the integration layer that maps GraphTask operations to scheduler jobs.
Validate functional equivalence with existing TaskGraphTest and TaskPipeTest suites.
non_goals: No behavior redesign of GraphEvent, GraphTask, TaskPipe, or user-facing task APIs in this checkpoint.
No new priority model, QoS policy, or affinity redesign beyond compatibility mapping of current priority tags.
No fallback dual backend or compatibility shim (latest-only replacement path).
No production code or test modification in this documentation-only PR.

strict_engineering_alignment: Latest-only implementation plan: replace old scheduler path instead of layering adapter/fallback paths.
No useless wrapper layers: Scheduler exposes only execution primitives, TaskGraph keeps dependency semantics.
Validation uses existing repository tests only (TaskGraphTest, TaskPipeTest, existing build/test scripts).
rule_codex_alignment: Do not add compatibility fallback implementation.
Avoid over-design; keep minimal scheduler/task boundary.
When reviewing runtime validation logs, focus on blocking errors.
Use PowerShell on Windows for existing script-based validation flows.

scheduler_job.description: Move-only executable unit consumed by scheduler workers. Created by TaskGraph when prerequisites become complete.
scheduler_job.invariant: A job is scheduler-visible only after TaskGraph has confirmed prerequisite completion; scheduler never evaluates graph dependencies.

worker_context.description: Per-worker state with one local Chase-Lev deque and park token.
worker_context.invariant: Owner thread performs push/pop at bottom; stealers access top only.

global_control.description: Shared epoch/notification state for waking sleeping workers and shutdown.
global_control.invariant: Wake decisions are independent from GraphEvent readiness details.

owner_push_bottom: If full, resize with lock (allocate larger buffer, copy [top, bottom), publish pointer/capacity).
owner_pop_bottom: If size > 0, return local task quickly.
If single element race, CAS top to claim or restore bottom on failure.
steal_top: Read slot at top, CAS top+1 to claim.

growth_policy.mechanism: Locked resize per worker deque is allowed; steady-state push/pop/steal remains lock-free.
growth_policy.memory_safety_note: Old buffers retired only after no concurrent stealers can read stale pointer (hazard-pointer/epoch/RCU strategy to be finalized in implementation checkpoint).

principles: Workers prioritize local pop, then bounded random steal attempts, then optional global fallback queue, then park.
Producer-side enqueue performs targeted notify (single or small batch) instead of bitmap scanning tied to fixed thread count.
Sleep/park primitive should use existing Event-based mechanism or condition variable abstraction already present in runtime platform layer.
wake_sleep_strategy.expected_effect: Remove fixed-width wake bitmap pressure and improve high-core load balancing under bursty task graphs.

requirements: WaitUntilTaskComplete on named thread keeps current pumping semantics (ProcessThreadUntilReturn/ReturnGraphTask logic unchanged at behavior level).
Named-thread local queue ordering and AnyThread dependency interactions remain equivalent to current tests.
named_thread_compatibility.non_interference_rule: AnyThread scheduler replacement must not alter named-thread task execution contracts observable by GraphTask/TaskPipe callers.

unchanged_upper_logic: TaskPipe chain linking and close/reopen behavior
replaceable_lower_logic: TaskThreadAnyThread fetch policy and idle behavior

migration_plan.title: Introduce Scheduler API and isolate TaskGraph backend calls
done_when: TaskGraph any-thread queue operations route through a narrow scheduler interface.
No GraphEvent types appear in scheduler headers.

migration_plan.title: Implement per-worker Chase-Lev deque with dynamic growth
done_when: Owner push/pop and steal operations follow Chase-Lev race rules.
Resize path supports growth safely, lock allowed on resize.

migration_plan.title: Replace atomic-flag/bitmap wake path with scalable notify/park flow
done_when: Worker wake no longer relies on fixed-width thread bitmap semantics.
Idle workers can park and resume without starvation under test load.

migration_plan.title: Keep named-thread behavior equivalent and enforce boundary tests
done_when: Named-thread waiting and return behavior passes existing tests unchanged.

migration_plan.title: Finalize legacy backend removal
done_when: Old any-thread scheduler backend is deleted (no fallback path).
TaskGraph uses new scheduler as single backend.

script_policy: Use existing repository test/build scripts only.
On Windows, run PowerShell scripts per repository convention.
No new ad-hoc validation wrappers for this change.
validation_plan.expected_result: All existing TaskGraphTest and TaskPipeTest assertions pass without test modifications.

risks.risk: Deque resize memory reclamation bug can cause stale pointer access by stealers.
risks.mitigation: Use explicit reclamation scheme (epoch or hazard pointer) and add stress validation under existing tests when possible.

risks.risk: Fairness regression where one busy worker hoards tasks and others underutilize.
risks.mitigation: Use bounded local batch and randomized stealing victim selection.

risks.risk: Named-thread wait semantics regress and reintroduce deadlock edge cases.
risks.mitigation: Do not change GraphEvent wait/return orchestration in this migration.

risks.risk: Over-coupling scheduler to TaskGraph internals during implementation.
risks.mitigation: Keep scheduler job contract free of GraphEventRef and GraphTask headers.

assumptions: Current upper-layer semantics are defined by existing behavior in TaskGraphTest and TaskPipeTest.
Performance targets are secondary to semantic equivalence in first replacement milestone.
Priority tags (high/normal/low) remain externally visible but can be implemented as scheduling hints instead of strict partitioned queues.

open_questions.question: Should AnyThread priorities remain strict isolation (3 pools) or become weighted hints on a unified stealable pool?
open_questions.impact: Affects fairness, starvation risk, and compatibility expectations for priority-sensitive workloads.

open_questions.question: Which memory reclamation strategy is preferred for old deque buffers after resize (epoch vs hazard pointer)?
open_questions.impact: Affects implementation complexity and runtime overhead.

open_questions.question: Do we require deterministic task execution order under equal-priority contention across workers, or only dependency correctness?
open_questions.impact: Affects steal policy and debug reproducibility.

open_questions.question: Should named-thread pumping remain entirely outside scheduler or use scheduler-assisted local pumping hooks?
open_questions.impact: Affects integration boundary complexity and ownership clarity.

acceptance_criteria: Design explicitly defines Chase-Lev work-stealing deque with dynamic growth.
Scheduler layer is documented as GraphEvent-independent.
Validation plan is based on existing TaskGraphTest and TaskPipeTest suites.
Document states strict-engineering and Rule_Codex alignment.
Checkpoint artifact is documentation-only and does not require production code/test changes in this PR.
